scenarios.context: Two friends talk about their summer holidays.

speakerA.en: Hi Dana! You look tanned. Where did you spend the summer?
Three weeks! That sounds amazing. What did you do every day?
Gardening? I thought you hated working outside.
Wow. Did you have any problems while you were there?
I'm sure that was hard for you. Did you get bored?
It sounds like the perfect holiday. I'd love to try it next year.

speakerB.en: Hi Leo! We went to my grandparents' village near the sea for three weeks.
In the mornings we swam, and in the afternoons I helped my grandfather in his garden.
I used to, but I learned a lot. We picked tomatoes and made jam together.
Only one. The Internet was terrible, so I couldn't message anyone.
Not at all. I read three books and played cards with my cousins every evening.
You should. Maybe you can come with us, and my grandfather will teach you to make jam.

scenarios.context: A girl tells her friend about getting lost.

speakerA.en: You look tired, Mina. What happened yesterday?
Lost? Didn't you have your phone with a map?
Oh no. What did you do next?
That sounds scary. Did you find your way in the end?
That was kind of him. Did you learn anything from it?
Good ideas. Next time, take a paper map as well.

speakerB.en: I got lost in the city centre. It was the strangest afternoon of my life.
The battery died just after I left the museum, and I didn't know the streets.
I tried asking people, but nobody spoke English, so I just walked and walked.
Yes. A shop owner let me charge my phone, and he even gave me a cup of tea.
I learned to carry a power bank and to learn a few words of the local language.
I'll do that. Actually, I'm going to buy one today.

scenarios.scenario: My first day at a new school
scenarios.context: A mother asks her daughter about her first day.

speakerA.en: Tell me everything about your first day at the new school, Sara.
I remember that feeling. Did you meet anyone nice?
That's lovely. What about the teachers?
And what was the hardest part of the day?
What did you do?
I'm so proud of you. It takes courage to start again somewhere new.

speakerB.en: Well, I was very nervous in the morning, and my stomach hurt on the bus.
Yes, a girl called Lina sat next to me and showed me around the school.
They seem friendly. The maths teacher said I could ask for help whenever I need it.
Lunch break. I didn't know where to sit, so I stood alone for a few minutes.
Lina saw me and invited me to join her group. By the end of the day I felt much better.
Thanks, Mum. I think tomorrow will be easier.

scenarios.context: A boy tells his friend about an embarrassing moment.

speakerA.en: You won't believe what happened to me at the supermarket today.
I saw a man who looked exactly like my uncle, so I ran up and hugged him.
He looked shocked and said, "Sorry, do I know you?" I was so embarrassed.
I said sorry and told him he looked just like my uncle. Then we both started laughing.
Yes, I phoned him right away. He said he would love to meet his twin.
Good idea! It's a story I'll tell for years.

speakerB.en: Go on, tell me. What happened?
You didn't! What did he do?
Oh no. What did you say?
At least he had a sense of humour. Did you tell your uncle afterwards?
That's hilarious. Maybe you should invite them both to dinner.
I'm sure it is. I'll never forget your face when you tell it.

scenarios.context: Two friends talk about learning a new skill.

speakerA.en: I heard you started learning the guitar. How is it going?
How long have you been learning?
Can you play any songs yet?
Do you have a teacher?
That's a good attitude. Are you thinking of performing in public someday?
I'm sure you'll do well. Please play something for me when you're ready.

speakerB.en: It's harder than I expected, but I really enjoy it.
About three months. I practise for half an hour every day after school.
Only simple ones. My fingers hurt when I play chords, but it's getting better.
Yes, a friendly man at the music school. He always says mistakes are part of learning.
Maybe at the school concert in spring, if I feel confident enough.
I will. You'll be the first person to hear my first full song.
